fields.title: 2.2 · The list is read again every three seconds, including while empty; a first project appears without restarting, unchanged reads leave the surface alone, and closing the page stops polling.

2.3 · Reopening follows the latest successful explicit project choice, whether made in the picker or by saying yes to setup. A newer picker choice supersedes an older setup choice, and a newer setup choice supersedes an older picker choice. `--project` wins on launch and becomes the remembered choice when that project exists. A remembered project that has gone falls back to the first; an unknown explicit project is named as missing.

2.4 · After a successful setup yes, the chosen project is durably recorded and becomes the project on show on the next refresh, or on reopening. The last successfully recorded yes wins even when several setups complete between reads or while the window is closed. A project-list read never overwrites an explicit choice, including one recorded while that read is in flight; discovering a name alone does not count as choosing it (ADR-0657 D3).
2.5 · With no projects, the app tells the user to start Claude Code or Codex in a folder and say yes when asked to set it up.

8.4 · In a folder that is not a project, the agent is told to ask the user, and nothing is created until the user says yes. A successful yes creates the project and folder marker, then durably records that project as the user's choice for the app. A refused or failed setup does not report success or change the remembered choice; if saving the choice fails, the folder marker is restored to its previous state so the explicit setup can be retried. An ordinary session start, an existing-project setup check, or a repeated setup tool call in an already configured folder records no choice. The setup prompt and tool input/output shapes remain the same (ADR-0657 D3).

fields.meaning:
- **As built** (`0-3-app-users-own-projects`, ADR-0657 D3): `set_up_project` passes the setup
  check's app home through to `setUpProject`; the default remains `STORYTREE_HOME`, else
  `~/.storytree/0.3`. Only the successful explicit setup path records a choice. `runSetupCheck` and
  the already-configured-folder return do not record one. `setup/setup-check.test.ts` contract 8.4
  exercises the real MCP tools against throwaway Postgres: no record before yes, none on a refused
  name, retry after a blocked choice destination, choice saved in the injected app home on success,
  and no choice change on existing-project checks, repeat tool calls or a new ordinary agent
  session.

- **As built** (`0-3-app-users-own-projects`, ADR-0657 D3): after opening the project's library and
  successfully writing its `.storytree.json` marker, `setUpProject` records the explicit choice
  through `routing/project-choice.ts`. A failed choice write restores the previous marker (or
  removes the newly created marker), so a later explicit yes can retry. The exported
  `readProjectChoice` / `recordProjectChoice` API shares one `project-choice.json` record with the
  app; each writer flushes its own uniquely named temporary file and atomically renames it into
  place. The app's existing dependency on agent-link supplies this seam without a reverse dependency
  or deep import. Routing to a project still depends only on the folder marker, independently of
  which project the app shows.

fields.title: 4.3 · After each update, the app that follows merged main checks its own verified health
fields.description: After restarting into a new merged-main build, the app runs `pnpm check:own-health` from that running slot in the background, against its own library. Its window and database remain available. The check joins the running app's database through `appLibraryServer` with `writes: true`, holding the writing lock so an update cannot restart the app while the check runs. The check's output and failures go to `~/.storytree/0.3/app.log` (or the same file under `STORYTREE_HOME`). A failed check never stops the app and is tried again at the next update. Reopening the same build does not repeat the attempt. This contract applies to the app that follows merged main; installed releases do not run checkout scripts.

fields.meaning:
- **As built** (`0-3-app-refreshes-own-health`): contract 4.3 is built in
  `packages/app/src/updates/own-health.ts`, called by the desktop's `followMain` only after database
  startup and window/tray setup in the newly running slot. `own-health.json` in the app home records
  the last attempted commit, including failures; a first launch with no record checks the current
  build. The child runs `pnpm check:own-health` with the slot as its working directory and the app's
  exact `STORYTREE_HOME`, forwarding both output streams to the app logger. Follow-main waits for
  the task before polling for another update, covering the interval before the child acquires the
  existing library writer lock. Installed release updates retain their existing behavior. Red-to-
  green proof is in `packages/app/src/updates/own-health.test.ts`; a real-database proof also
  verified that the command joins the app, holds/releases the updater's writer lock, updates
  verified health, and preserves reported health.

fields.title: Storytree 0.3's own library: its stories and decisions, before cutover
fields.intent:
*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this arc was `storytree-0-3-own-library-arc`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

**Put storytree 0.3's own work and knowledge into 0.3's own library, so that the project cutover runs on is not empty.** Today the only loader, the 0.3 repo's `pnpm seed:library-story` (renamed `pnpm seed:library` by storytree-ai/storytree#18), puts the library story alone into the 0.3 app's `storytree` project. The agent-link story is not loaded, and neither is any decision or note, so every shelf is empty. Nothing in the plan filled it: cutover (ADR-0625 step 4) says the plan moves in, not the knowledge.

**Why this arc exists (2026-09-26, owner-directed).** The owner asked: "Dont we need to populate the library?" He also asked for the MVP arc to be split so that more sessions can work at once: "feels like [that arc] needs to be broken up more, like I would of assumed we could have more parrallel sessions working on this using separate arcs". A lobby session in the primary checkout (desktop title "Storytree 0.3 MVP arc breakdown") surveyed the plan and put three choices to him. Its store writes carry no branch, because the primary checkout has no ledger identity. He SELECTED these options, which that session composed: "Split as drawn (Recommended)", "Draft all 3 now, answer 1 at a time (Recommended)" and "Only what was decided for 0.3 (Recommended)". They are labels he clicked, not his words. The last one sets this arc's scope, and he was shown it as: "Both story files, plus each new one as it lands. Then the eight or so 0.3 decisions, each filed as the cover of the part it decided, and the plan itself at cutover."

**Scope.**
- Every story file (`stories/*.md` in the 0.3 repo), plus each new one as it lands.
- The decisions made for 0.3, each filed as a front cover of the story or part it decided (ADR-0627). Each takes 0.3's short form: a title, the decision in plain words, and a pointer to the full record in storytree02's store.
- The plan itself (the lane arcs, as 0.3 arcs: lists of stories) is loaded at cutover by `0-3-cutover-builds-itself`, using this arc's loader. It stays with cutover, so that this arc and cutover do not wait on each other.

**Not in scope.** 0.2's corpus, and users' projects. Users' projects still start nearly empty by design (ADR-0621 D6), and their agents fill them.

**A known open point.** Some 0.3 decisions cover the whole project rather than one story or part: the MVP spec (ADR-0625), minimal viable TDD (ADR-0623) and the license (ADR-0617). Under ADR-0627 every front cover covers exactly one node, so these have no shelf. Put that to the owner as a question on this arc when you reach it. Do not invent a project shelf. *(Answered 2026-09-26: ADR-0631, option A. They load on no shelf, and 0.3's librarian draws their links once it is set up.)*

**Why now rather than at cutover.** It waits on nothing: the library and its front covers are built. It touches only the 0.3 repo's seed scripts and the app's data. And it gives the forest and the arc surface a real project to show while they are being built.

**Cutover waits on this arc** (`0-3-cutover-builds-itself`, on `trusted-circle-distribution-arc`).

Each decision made for 0.3 is a front cover of the story or part it decided, or sits wherever the owner rules a project-wide decision lives. A repeatable command loads it all, updating in place and never duplicating.

fields.title: A planet-shaped forest with the knowledge graph in its core
fields.intent:
*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this arc was `planet-forest-knowledge-core-arc`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

**The intent.** **Owner concept, 2026-09-26, DECIDED the same day: 0.3's forest becomes a planet (ADR-0629).** The globe (`0-3-planet`) is built. The knowledge core is built now, in parallel with the MVP (ADR-0647 D3, the owner, 2026-09-27: "build it in parrallel doesnt need to wait until MVP is done"). *(Corrected in place 2026-09-27. This used to say the planet ranks below every 0.3 MVP increment, never runs ahead of the MVP, and is taken only when no MVP lane can run (ADR-0629 D3); ADR-0647 D3 retires that ranking for the core.)*

The owner's words, verbatim: *"One of the ideas I want to explore is to reshape the forest to be applied to a sphere, like a planet. The reason i want to do this is it allows us to create a core which you can peek into in the gaps between the islands. inside this core I want to build a way to visualise the knowledge graph. The way I imagine the knowledge corpus is each storynode (probably more like its capabilities in where we want to move to) there are the entrypoints to the graph so story nodes have the entrance points to the rabbit hole and so these entrace points chain toward the core of the plant in a 3d node graph. I know 0.3 is mvp but i want to explore this concept in parrallel and so when we have spare tokens and can't run any more parallel build lanes we can explore this concet. ... this would replace the context traversal and so as sessions explore the knowledge corpus we can light up the nodes on a color that matches and they can leave a color trace so I can see where they hit."*

**The picture.** The 0.3 forest's islands sit on the surface of a sphere. The sea between them is see-through, so the core glows through the gaps. Each capability is an entrance: the knowledge linked to it hangs just under its island, and chains of references lead down toward the core. When a session reads knowledge, those notes light up in the session's own colour and leave a fading trail. 0.3's MVP leaves context traversal out, so in 0.3 this would be the first view of where agents go in the knowledge; what it replaces is 0.2's replay panel.

**Why it fits.**
1. It makes the owner's pitch line literal: *"you choose which rabbit hole to jump into and how far to go down"* (ADR-0442). It also matches his 0.2 model of the library as a set of rabbit holes (ADR-0476).
2. 0.3's knowledge store already has this shape. Each story and capability has a shelf of front-cover decisions, and notes link to other notes, so chains of references lead down from the shelves (ADR-0627, built as `0-3-library-knowledge-entrances`). *(Corrected in place 2026-09-26: this line used to say a note can link to any record, a story or capability included, which ADR-0627 D3 overtook.)*
3. 0.3 projects start nearly empty, so the core holds tens to a few hundred notes, a size a 3D graph can show legibly. 0.2's ~750 knowledge artifacts are the stress test.

**What decides whether it works. Read this before building anything; each point is a lesson 0.2 measured.**
1. **The roots must exist.** 0.2 measured depth from the stories and capabilities (ADR-0363 D2) and could reach only a minority of the knowledge (re-measured on 2026-09-26 with `pnpm probe:depth-from-work`: 232 of 615 decisions, or 38%), because most of it was tied to no piece of work. That is why ADR-0476 moved the 0.2 panel to seeding from the graph's own surface. In 0.3 the cheap fix is at write time: when a session has claimed a capability, a note it writes links to that capability by default. **DECIDED 2026-09-26 (ADR-0624 D2).**
   - *Redirected the same day by ADR-0627, the owner's rabbit-hole model.* Each story and capability has a SHELF of front-cover decisions, and each decision covers one node only. Notes link only to other notes.
   - So a new decision lands on the claimed capability's shelf, and a new memory or definition lands inside the cover the session last opened there.
   - For the planet, every front cover has exactly ONE home island, and the shelves are the entrances into the core.
   - *Measurement note:* the probe's 232 counts only routes that start at increments. Walking 0.2's own `decisions:` lists as well reaches 338 of 616 (55%).
2. **Lighting needs a record of READS, and that record cannot be backfilled.** 0.3's library keeps a history of every write and no reads. The agent link (`0-3-agent-link`) is where each knowledge read is recorded; its builder reported on 2026-09-26 that the first build shipped the record: which session, which note, how it was found (search, from another note, by id), and whether it was a peek or a full read. 0.2 could not recover what it had not recorded: ADR-0541 D5 declined a backfill that could not be bought. **DECIDED 2026-09-26: both this record and point 1's default link go into the MVP** (ADR-0624; the owner: "sure go with A"). They are written onto `0-3-agent-link`, and `oq-0-3-agent-link-records-knowledge-reads` is settled. **Extended the same day by ADR-0629 D2:** each read also names the agent that made it, the orchestrator or a subagent by its type and task, as an optional field that says "unknown" when the harness does not reveal it.
3. **Depth must mean ONE thing: how far down a chain of references a note sits from the work, counted by the LONGEST chain.** ADR-0476 D2 measured that a shortest-route reading squashes every node into the top two or three layers. The longest chain also keeps point 1's default links from flattening the planet (under ADR-0627, a decision placed by default sits one step below its capability, and a note two): a note linked straight to a capability still sits deep if a longer chain reaches it. Artifacts reached from no shelf have NO depth. On the globe they pool in a small cluster at the centre (ADR-0658 D2); this position does not assign them depth or mean "most foundational". *(Narrowed in place 2026-09-27 by ADR-0658: this originally required an outside orbit, following 0.2's unmeasured-row lesson, ADR-0482 / ADR-0511; the retained, unmounted Look-inside view still uses that orbit.)* How widely a note is shared is a different quantity, so show it as size, never as depth (ADR-0476 D4: two readings are never summed). The knowledge graph refuses loops (ADR-0647 D2, L3): the library refuses a link that would close one (`0-3-library-refuses-loops`), and until that lands the core draws any loop it meets as a labelled error, never a supported shape.
4. **Never draw a walk that did not happen.** 0.2 recorded how a read was reached on about 6% of reads. An agent that searched straight to a deep note plotted exactly like one that crawled down to it. A trail line runs along an edge only where the capture recorded a followed link; every other move is drawn as a jump.
5. **The trail shows REACH, never usefulness.** It also covers only the reads that went through storytree's own tools, never the code an agent read directly. ADR-0548 closed "was this knowledge useful?" as unobservable; do not re-open it here.
6. **A globe shows one side at a time.** Triage is pushed and investigation is pulled (ADR-0442 D5), so a failing island must never be hidden on the far side: either the planet turns toward what needs attention, or a flat overview stays one click away. Peeking into the core works best as a deliberate move, a dive through a gap or a cutaway, because from orbit the near islands block the core and the far islands show through the gaps.
7. **Judge it by what the owner would DO after looking.** 0.2's replay panel paid for itself once, when it disproved the owner's model of how agents move through the knowledge, and then had little left to say (`replay-answers-retrieval-ease-arc`). Candidate actions for the planet: prune knowledge nobody reaches, notice agents going unusually deep, spot notes tied to no work, and see two sessions converging on the same knowledge. If none of these would change what he does, it is decoration.

**Scope fence.** The owner let exactly three things into the 0.3 MVP: point 2's record, the agent named on each read (ADR-0629 D2), and point 1's default link (ADR-0624). Nothing else here enters it. The prototype touches neither repo. The planet won (ADR-0629 D1), so each island will be placed on a sphere instead of on a plane. That switch is cheapest if the MVP forest (`0-3-forest`) keeps placement as one function from story to position, which the forest's own review puts to the owner.

**The build (ADR-0629 D3 and D4).** Two 0.3 stories, each preceded by an owner capability-tree review, taken one at a time (ADR-0625 D5):
- `0-3-planet`, the globe: the forest's placement on a sphere, a see-through sea, and point 6's rule that a failing island is never hidden.
- `0-3-knowledge-core`, the knowledge inside it: depth from the shelves (point 3, with a stated rule for loops), replaced decisions as ghosts, and recorded reads lit per agent (points 4 and 5).
A ghost comes from the library's decision log, which returned with explicit supersession (ADR-0640), plus the older write-history recipe labelled "earlier cover" (ADR-0647, pick G2). Proposed ghosts are deferred. *(Corrected in place 2026-09-27: this used to say 0.3's library carries no decision status, which ADR-0640 overtook.)* The prototype's four versions (this arc's log) are the reference for the look, not a specification.
fields.endState:
Closed when a 0.3 project's forest can be shown as a planet: its islands on a sphere with a see-through sea, a failing island never hidden on the far side, and the project's knowledge hanging inside as a core that recorded reads light per agent. It is built as the owner-approved capability trees of `0-3-planet` and `0-3-knowledge-core` say, after the 0.3 forest, with the core built in parallel with the MVP (ADR-0629, ADR-0647 D3). If a review or the build shows the planet does not read on real 0.3 data, the arc closes with the owner's reason instead.

*(Rewritten 2026-09-26 when the owner decided, ADR-0629. It used to read: closed when the owner has walked a working prototype and decided whether 0.3's forest becomes a planet. He walked four versions and said yes, which met that end state and turned this arc into the planet's build.)*
fields.description: Explore reshaping the 0.3 forest onto a planet whose core shows the knowledge graph, lit where sessions read. Spare capacity only, below the MVP.

fields.title: 0.3's decisions can't take their 0.2 numbers: the library refuses to change a number once set
fields.stakes: Until this is settled, 0.3's decisions carry numbers that mean something different in 0.2. In 0.3, "ADR-0001" is project routing; in 0.2 it is an unrelated decision. That is the confusion your N1 choice was meant to prevent. There is also a live collision: the next decision 0.3 records on its own is numbered one past its highest, and once any decision holds 0659, that next one is 0660, which 0.2 already gave to the Forest / Library toggle decision today. Nothing is broken for the app itself; the forest, the arc surface and the library all work.
fields.analogy: It is like a company merging two filing systems where files keep their original case numbers. The new cabinet was built to accept a case number only when a file is first put in, and it glues the label on after that. The movers loaded every file without its label, so the cabinet stamped its own numbers. Option A is a supervised relabelling that happens once, checked against the paperwork inside each file. Option B is photocopying each file under the right number, shredding the original, and updating every cross-reference that pointed at it. Option C leaves the labels as they are until the old cabinet is shut. Where it breaks: a real cabinet can peel a label off; this library also remembers every number a file has ever had, so a wrong relabel cannot simply be reversed.
fields.context:
Measured 2026-09-27 against your running 0.3 app library (all 82 decisions read and saved before anything was tried):
- **29 decisions** name their 0.2 record in a "Full record: ADR-NNNN" line: ADR-0617, 0621, 0623 to 0627, 0629 to 0632, 0634, 0635, 0637, 0638, 0640, 0642 to 0648, 0650, 0655, 0656, 0658, 0659, plus one naming ADR-0169 (routed pathways, the 0.2 decision it ports). None of those numbers has ever been held in 0.3's library, so none would collide. 13 of the 29 are unnumbered today and 16 hold a local number.
- **53 decisions** are "founding books": short rules written for 0.3's own capabilities (for example "1 · Project routing: founding book"). They have no 0.2 record of their own, so N1 gives them no 0.2 number to keep. Under N1 they would need numbers above 0.2's highest, and 0.2 is still recording decisions today (ADR-0660 was filed this evening), so numbering them now could collide later. N1 itself says the collision risk ends at cutover, when 0.2 becomes read-only.
- Why the flip missed it: the old loader (`pnpm seed:library`) never learned to read numbers out of files. ADR-0641 D3 deliberately left that for a later "one edit" (D2 step 5), not knowing the library would refuse an edit to a number.
- The library refuses any number that any record has EVER held, so a mistake cannot be undone by renumbering back.
fields.options:
**A. Add a one-time numbering command for this move (recommended).** A small 0.3 change, tested red then green: a command that gives an already-loaded decision its 0.2 number, only in the `storytree` project, only a number no record has ever held, and only for a decision whose own "Full record" line names that number. The 29 get their 0.2 numbers now; the 53 founding books keep their local numbers until cutover and are renumbered above 0.2's final number then. The rule "a number never changes" stays true for everything else.
- For: does exactly what N1 promised, and every change is checked against the decision's own text. The library's history keeps each old number.
- Against: it is an exception to a rule the library was built on, so it has to be kept narrow. It also costs one build lane (about an hour).

**B. Re-record the 29 with their numbers, and retire the old records.** No code change: `adr new` accepts a number when a decision is first recorded.
- For: uses only what exists today.
- Against: stories, capabilities and other decisions point at the old records by their id (front covers, supersedes, links), so each of those links must be moved as well. That is about 29 new records, 29 retirements and every link that points at them, which is a much larger edit to your live library with more room for error.

**C. Keep the local numbers, and apply N1 only from cutover on.**
- For: nothing to do now.
- Against: until cutover, "ADR-0050" means one thing in 0.3 and another in 0.2, which is what N1 ruled out. The collision at 0660 still has to be handled when 0.3 records its first decision of its own.
fields.statement:
*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this question was `oq-0-3-decision-numbers-refused`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

Your N1 choice (ADR-0640 D3) says a decision number means one thing across 0.2 and 0.3, so a 0.3 decision recorded in 0.2's log keeps its 0.2 number (ADR-0621 stays 0621). The library was built to apply that only when a decision is FIRST loaded: "a decision brought in with its own number keeps it", and after that "a decision's number never changes" (0.3's library, capability 13). The flip that made the library the one copy of 0.3's stories and decisions (storytree-ai/storytree#118) loaded all 82 decisions without their 0.2 numbers, so the library handed out its own, 1 to 69. The planned follow-up edit (increment `0-3-library-decision-numbers`) is therefore refused by design: `library edit decision_229b7f7d10de --number 658` answers "editNote does not change "number": a decision's number never changes". Nothing was changed. How should 0.3's decisions get their 0.2 numbers now?
fields.recommendation: Non-binding: A. It keeps your N1 promise with the smallest and best-checked change, and it leaves the 53 founding books for cutover, which N1 already names as the moment 0.2 stops handing out numbers. B moves far more of your live library to get the same result.

fields.body:
*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this increment was `0-3-arc-surface`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

Port the arc view from 0.2 behaviourally, without increments: in 0.3 an arc is a list of stories (ADR-0625 D8). Claims give the live who-is-on-what. The project switcher belongs to the 0.3 app story (ADR-0632 D4), whose frame hosts both the arc surface and the forest.

**Signed spec (ADR-0625, 2026-09-26).**
- Built third, after the agent link and verified health (D6).
  - *Corrected 2026-09-26 by ADR-0630: the owner dropped verified health from the MVP, so this story now follows the agent link alone.*
  - *Moved 2026-09-26 (owner-directed lane split) to its own arc, `storytree-0-3-arc-surface-arc`, whose first increment is this story's capability-tree review. In the signed diagram it reads only the library and the agent link's sessions and claims, not verified health, so the two can be built side by side.*
- Read-only. Per project it shows what is planned, what is in progress right now and by which agent, and what landed. Each story's state is derived from the records, never typed in.
- *Uses:* `projectTree`, `arcsFor`, `changesSince`, `listProjects`, and the sessions and claims from the agent link. They are kept in the agent link's own agent activity log, beside the library (decided by ADR-0626 D2).
- It gets its own capability-tree review before any code (D5).

**One 0.2 render not to port** (observed 2026-09-26). `storytree arc show` printed two lines for the same increment, which was waiting on the owner:
- "held, not work to take until that is settled";
- "⚠ `active` but NO claim holds it … Takeable".

A row waiting on the owner must never also read as takeable.

**Approved 2026-09-27 (ADR-0638); who builds what, as dispatched that day.** The owner approved the tree ("approved, please cut fresh sessions for all work on 0.3 that can now proceed"). The build may start, in two parts:
- **Now, by the forest lane** (session "Build the 0.3 forest (caps 2–6) and shared Work states", under ADR-0632 D3's shared-piece rule): this story's first landing (`stories/arc-surface.md`, `decisions/arc-surface-capability-tree.md`), capability 1 Work states at PART grain, and the live reading (part of capability 3), kept in the arc surface story's package. Do not start these a second time.
- **Later, a session of its own:** increment and arc grain of Work states, capabilities 2 (Agents on the board), 3's overlay itself, 4 (Waits) and 5 (Briefing). They need the library's and agent link's revised trees (`0-3-library-tree-for-adr-0633`, `0-3-agent-link-tree-for-adr-0633`) approved and built first.

**Built by the forest lane, 2026-09-27** (merged, not squashed; storytree-ai/storytree):
- **#35:** `stories/arc-surface.md` (the five capabilities, their shelves and 23 contracts, as ADR-0638 approved them) and `decisions/arc-surface-capability-tree.md` (ADR-0638 as the story's front cover). **Capability 1 · Work states at PART grain** (contracts 1.1–1.3) in the new package `packages/arc-surface` (`@storytree/arc-surface`): `workStates(lines)`, a pure function of the agent activity log's lines — a part is planned until claimed, in progress from its first claim until a landed line (a release or a closed window leaves it in progress, B1), landed on a landed line, in progress again on a later claim; a story follows its parts. It imports only types, so the page bundles it. `pnpm test-ratio` all: 6,342 / 5,624, 1.13.
- **#37:** **the live reading** (part of capability 3): `liveReading({ project, reads, onNews, onClock, onError, timers })` — reads everything at once, then about every 2 s asks `changesSince`/`linesSince` from where it got to (each cursor carried forward), hands on only what is new, re-reads the clock once a minute regardless, reports a failed read and retries from the same place, one ask at a time, never writes. Tested with a stand-in clock; contracts 3.4/3.5 (in-app) are proved when the overlay is drawn. `pnpm test-ratio` all: 6,466 / 5,693, 1.14.
- **Not built, left for this story's own session:** increment and arc grains of Work states (1.4–1.6), capabilities 2, 3's overlay (3.1–3.6), 4 and 5 — they wait for the library's and agent link's revised trees. The forest consumes `workStates` (its capability 2) and `liveReading` (its capability 3) from `@storytree/arc-surface`; extend them there rather than forking a copy.
fields.title: 0.3 arc surface

outcome.note:
All remaining arc-surface contracts landed in storytree-ai/storytree: #101 Work states at increment and arc grain (1.4–1.6); #103 Agents on the board (2.1–2.4); #105 Waits (4.1–4.4); #108 Briefing (5.1–5.3); #112 the read-only overlay and in-app proofs (3.1–3.6). These extend the original #35 part states and #37 live reading in packages/arc-surface. The desktop mounts the package view over the forest, carries public library reads, and invokes its smoke check. The collision fence was respected; no forest-folder mount remainder is left.

Each capability followed committed red then green, with every commit pushed and CI merging each non-draft PR after Linux, macOS and Windows passed. Final local verification passed typechecking and all 12 test units under the heavy lock. Actual desktop-renderer acceptance with isolated Postgres and headless Chromium verified live claims (1.84 s), clock-only idle, retries, every lifecycle scope, preserved question folds/scroll, live settlement, read-only actions, and returning to the same forest on Close/Escape. Evidence is in packages/arc-surface/evidence; the lane report is /tmp/arc-surface-report.md. No product work remains in this increment. fields.body:
*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this increment was `planet-forest-knowledge-core-arc-inc-01`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

**The owner's go-ahead, 2026-09-26:** *"cut a fresh session to prototype this for me using our corpus, something that shows me what this could look like."* The job is to SHOW him the look on real data: build for the picture, and label it honestly.

**What it is.** One standalone page (three.js from a CDN). It makes no change to 0.2, which is frozen, so commit nothing there, and none to the 0.3 repo. Publish it as a private artifact page or serve it as a local file. Keep its source and the data-export script under `~/.storytree/prototypes/planet-core/` so a later session can iterate on it. Hand over a link you have confirmed works (`stage-the-attestation-experience`).

**What it shows.**
- Islands on a sphere, one per live 0.2 story, with gaps between them. The sea is see-through, so the core glows through.
- Two ways into the core: a dive through a gap, and a cutaway that slices the planet open.
- The knowledge graph inside:
  - radius shows depth, and deeper means nearer the core;
  - each note sits under the islands that reach it, where any do;
  - size shows how widely a note is shared;
  - notes with no edges orbit outside the planet, never at the core.
- Real sessions' reads replayed as light, each session in its own colour, with a fading trail. Jumps are drawn as jumps, never as walks along edges.

**Data: our corpus (0.2's live store), knowledge tiers only.**
- **Nodes.** Knowledge artifacts only: decisions, principles, definitions, patterns, guardrails, processes and agents. Exclude the record tiers (`RECORD_KINDS` in `packages/library/src/surface-depth.ts`: increments, friction, arcs, open questions, templates). Allow-list the exported fields (id, kind, title) and never export bodies.
- **Depth.** Most of 0.2's knowledge is NOT tied to any story or capability (`evaluateDepthFromWork` reaches only a minority of it), so measuring depth from the work would leave most of the core empty. For this prototype, draw the graph's own surface depth with `evaluateSurfaceDepth` (ADR-0476: the longest chain over `dependsOn`, with decision twins collapsed). `pnpm probe:surface-depth` prints its figures. Reuse it and never write a second graph walker, because a naive one inverts the decision tier (the decision-twin trap). Say on screen which depth is drawn, and that 0.3 would measure it from the capabilities, since ADR-0624 ties notes to them by default.
- **Islands.** Live stories and their capabilities. Where a knowledge node carries a work anchor (it names a story or capability), place it under that island; otherwise place it near its linked neighbours.
- **Trails.** Use 2–4 real session traces from `~/.storytree/traces/*.jsonl` that contain many knowledge reads. Prefer traces whose lines carry `grade: "window"`, which covers one context window each; older slot-keyed traces pool many windows together. `pnpm storytree traversal show <session>` renders a trace as text, and `replayTraversalSessionAllAdapters()` in `packages/context-traversal-spawn/src/replay-adapters.ts` composes the structured replay. 0.2 recorded how a read was reached on only about 6% of reads, so nearly every move is a jump; draw it that way.
- **Optional, if cheap.** A view that shows only one story's neighbourhood, to approximate what a young 0.3 project would look like.

**The four questions the owner's look answers.**
1. At a glance, can you tell what is happening, or does the globe hide too much?
2. Is peeking through the gaps enough, or do you want the dive or the cutaway?
3. Is the 3D graph readable at our corpus's size?
4. Does a lit trail tell you where a session hit, and would you act on what it shows?

**Fence.** One session. This is a prototype for answering questions, not the 0.3 forest: no art research, no land treatment, plain materials. Put the owner's look to him as an open question on this arc, with the link and a screenshot. Then close this increment with a note on what was built, and end.
fields.title: Build a throwaway, interactive prototype of the planet from real data that the…

outcome.note:
**Built and published** the planet prototype from 0.2's corpus: https://claude.ai/artifact/RSeesuTgNM7Xy9aALgN2Sz (private, version 2). The source, data export and README are in `~/.storytree/prototypes/planet-core/`, which is outside both repos; nothing was committed to 0.2 or 0.3. Verified in the Browser pane against a local copy of the same file, at desktop and phone width: orbit, dive, cutaway, trail playback, hover and pin, one-story view, and colour modes, with no console errors. The pane cannot open the private link because it is not signed in to claude.ai.

**What it draws.**
- 36 live stories as islands, with their 225 capabilities as patches.
- 874 knowledge notes (the brief's seven kinds plus the tech-stack notes) and the 1,855 links between them.
- Radius is 0.2's surface depth: `evaluateSurfaceDepth`, fed exactly as `probe:surface-depth` feeds it, 31 levels deep. Size is how many artifacts point at a note. The 7 notes with no links orbit outside.
- Placement under islands comes from `evaluateDepthFromWork`, run once per live story and per live capability.
- Trails replay the four single-window sessions that read the most notes. A read is drawn as a walk only where the trace carries a recorded parent read; everything else is a jump.

**What it showed.**
- Only 241 of 874 notes (28%) can be reached from any story's work. No knowledge note names a story or capability itself; every route runs through an increment. This confirms the gap ADR-0624 closes.
- 70% of notes sit in the top four depth layers.
- In these four trails, 174 of 866 reads are recorded walks, and every one is an agent pulling in its standing rules.
- Only 60 notes were never read in any of the 1,228 sessions captured on this laptop.

The owner's look is put to him as `oq-planet-prototype-look`. Acting on his answer is parked as `-inc-02`, which waits on that question.

fields.body:
*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this increment was `planet-forest-knowledge-core-arc-inc-02`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

**Waits on `oq-planet-prototype-look`.** The owner walks the prototype at https://claude.ai/artifact/RSeesuTgNM7Xy9aALgN2Sz (private to him) and answers the four questions from inc-01's brief, then decides whether 0.3's forest becomes a planet. Nothing here can start before he answers, and a session must not answer for him.

**Why this row exists.** inc-01 built the prototype and closed. This arc's end state is closed only when the owner has walked the prototype AND decided. With no open increment, the mechanical lifecycle (ADR-0335) would close the arc while his look was still pending. This row keeps the decision's follow-through on the arc.

**When he answers, in this order:**
1. Record a real decision (yes or no) as an ADR, stamped `--arc planet-forest-knowledge-core-arc`. Record "not yet" in the answer alone.
2. Settle the question with his words: `storytree question settle oq-planet-prototype-look --answer <his words> [--adr <n>] --pg`.
3. Then act on the answer:
   - **Yes:** park the build work here as new increments. One goes against `0-3-forest`: islands placed on a sphere, with placement kept as a single function from story to position. One goes against a knowledge view fed by the agent link's read record (ADR-0624). Every one ranks below every 0.3 MVP increment and never runs ahead of the MVP.
   - **No:** close this increment with his reason. The arc then closes itself.
   - **Not yet:** write the revisit trigger into this row, for example a real 0.3 project with a few weeks of recorded reads. Then park the arc (ADR-0374) so it holds without reading as in flight.

**The prototype, if it needs another pass.** The source is at `~/.storytree/prototypes/planet-core/`, and its `README.md` covers the pipeline: export (needs a 0.2 checkout and the live store), then build, serve and shoot. It is throwaway and lives in neither repo.

Spare capacity only (arc intent): take this only when no 0.3 MVP lane can run.

**Also waits on `oq-0-3-read-record-names-the-agent`** (filed 2026-09-26 in pass 2). It asks whether 0.3's read record should also name the agent, orchestrator or subagent, that made each read. If the answer is yes: record the decision, settle that question with his words, write the optional agent field onto `0-3-agent-link` as part of the ADR-0624 D1 record, and annotate ADR-0624 in place, because D1's field list narrows. If no, settle it with his reason; nothing else changes.
fields.title: Act on the owner's look at the planet prototype

outcome.note:
**The owner answered both questions on 2026-09-26: "yes and yes".** Recorded as ADR-0629, and both questions are settled with his words.
- `oq-planet-prototype-look`: yes (option A). 0.3's forest becomes a planet, ranked below every MVP increment.
- `oq-0-3-read-record-names-the-agent`: yes (option A). Each read also names its agent, as an optional field. ADR-0624 D1 is annotated in place.

**His instruction was to review the existing arcs and add what the planet needs**, with its own arc if that made sense and a dependency on the 0.3 forest arc. Four read-only reviewers covered the forest, the agent link, the library, and 0.3's scope rules. What came of it:
- **The planet keeps this arc** (ADR-0629 D4). Its intent and end state now describe the build, and it is queued behind `storytree-0-3-forest-arc` with an arc gate, so it cannot start until the 0.3 forest is built.
- **Four increments are parked here:** `-inc-05` (owner review of `0-3-planet`'s tree), `0-3-planet` (the globe), `-inc-06` (owner review of `0-3-knowledge-core`'s tree, after `-inc-05`), and `0-3-knowledge-core` (the knowledge inside it).
- **The agent field** is parked by the agent link's builder as `0-3-agent-link-read-record-names-the-agent` on `trusted-circle-distribution-arc`, inside the MVP. That build had already shipped the read record without the field. ADR-0629 D2, the ADR-0624 annotation and the settled answer say so.
- **The forest's review session** was told the planet is decided; the forest's tree stays the owner's to approve there.
- **Nothing else changes in the MVP.** 0.3's library needs no status field: the planet finds replaced decisions in its write history (ADR-0621 D6 stands), and 0.3 has no proposed state, so there are no proposed ghosts.

fields.objective: When the owner answers `oq-planet-prototype-look`, settle it with his words and do what the answer says: park the planet build work on this arc (yes), close the arc with his reason (no), or record what should trigger the next look (not yet).

fields.body:
*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this increment was `planet-forest-knowledge-core-arc-inc-03`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

**The owner's first look, 2026-09-26, in his words:** *"This looks really good, needs a few iterations but is a great start. I think just like our storynodes, links only show when you select a node - else its way too noisy. one orchestration session at a time else too noisy, this way we can have colors for it and all its subagents. should have options not to show this and only show the islands and also hide the islands, one toggle forest -> library -> both (default). Do we really have this many active ADRs? theres so many nodes more than expected, just want to double check are we hiding superceded nodes? I'd expect us to only show active ones."*

**This pass, all in `~/.storytree/prototypes/planet-core/`, republished to the same link:**
1. **Links show only for the selected note**, as on the story map.
2. **One orchestration session at a time**, picked from a list. The orchestrator gets one colour, and each of its subagents gets its own. The read traces do not record which subagent made a read, because a subagent's CLI calls log under its parent's session. So each read is attributed by matching it to the Claude Code transcript command that ran it (the parent's, or a subagent's own `subagents/agent-*.jsonl`), and reads that cannot be tied to one agent are shown as unattributed rather than guessed.
3. **One toggle: Forest, Library, Both** (Both is the default).
4. **Active knowledge only.** The count the owner doubted is real: the store holds 616 decisions, of which 551 are current (accepted and not superseded, the `adr list --current` rule), 55 superseded and 10 proposed. Pass 1 drew all of them. This pass drops the 65 that are not current, and computes depth over the drawn notes only.

Acting on his eventual yes / no / not yet stays with `-inc-02`, which waits on `oq-planet-prototype-look`.
fields.title: Prototype pass 2 from the owner's first look

outcome.note:
**Pass 2 is published as version 3** of https://claude.ai/artifact/RSeesuTgNM7Xy9aALgN2Sz, the same private link. The source and README are in `~/.storytree/prototypes/planet-core/`, and nothing was committed to 0.2 or 0.3. It was checked in the Browser pane against a local copy of the same file: the layer toggle, pinning a note, switching sessions, the per-agent tick boxes and the cutaway, with no console errors.

**What changed, per the owner's first look:**
- Links show only for the pinned note.
- One session plays at a time, picked by its desktop title. The orchestrator is always blue, and each subagent takes the next colour of a colour-blind-checked fixed order.
- A Forest / Library / Both toggle is added.
- Only active knowledge is drawn: 810 notes, with the 551 current decisions of 616 (55 superseded and 10 proposed dropped). Depth is computed over the drawn notes only; the deepest chain is 29 (ADR-0036).

**What it showed:**
- The read traces file a subagent's CLI reads under its parent session, so a read is tied to an agent by matching it to the command in Claude Code's transcripts that ran it (`attribute.mjs`). Seven of the eight sessions tie 88% to 98% of their reads to one agent. The one with six parallel subagents ties 52%, and its remaining reads are drawn grey and never guessed.
- In the default session, "Art arcs/3D render open questions", an explorer subagent read 102 notes and reached depth 19, while the orchestrator itself read 9.
- 0.3's read record (ADR-0624) would carry the agent directly.

The owner's four points are captured as re-steers: three taste, and one defect (superseded and proposed decisions were drawn). `oq-planet-prototype-look`'s context and recommendation are updated to version 3. Acting on his yes / no / not yet stays with `-inc-02`.

fields.objective: Rework the planet prototype on the owner's first look: links only for the selected note, one orchestration session at a time with a colour per subagent, a Forest / Library / Both toggle, and active knowledge only.

fields.body:
*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this increment was `planet-forest-knowledge-core-arc-inc-04`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

**The owner's second look, 2026-09-26, in his words:** *"How can we have so many active decisions and so few superceded, wouldnt the active decisions start to conflict with each other or pull against each other - guess it depends on granulaity - in 0.3 since we would anchor the decisions to a story i imagine the shape would be dense close to the story (since these would be specific) and then sparse in the shared spaces between the stories. For superceded and proposed I think we make these transparent so they still light up if the agent visited them, else we should color all the nodes a grey nutral somthing faded to make the graph less noisy. What does a node size represent? i would of imagined it represents how frequently the node is visited. Also i think if an agent only read the front matter/abstract then we dont draw an edge just color the node."*

**The four changes for pass 3.** Work in `~/.storytree/prototypes/planet-core/` and read its `README.md` first.
1. **Superseded and proposed decisions come back as ghosts.** Draw them transparent (about 20% opacity), and have them light up in the reading agent's colour when a session visits one.
   - Export them with a state of `superseded` or `proposed`, plus `supersededBy`: invert the `supersedes` numbers that `loadTitledAdrMetasFromStore` returns. This is the same read `adr list` makes, already imported in `export-corpus.mts`.
   - Keep ACTIVE depth computed over active notes only. A ghost needs a position: place a superseded decision beside its replacement, and a proposed one near what it links to.
   - The card says "superseded by ADR-NNNN".
   - "Chapter 2 archival and MVP rebuild" has 43 reads of such decisions, which are skipped today. Use it to check that ghosts light.
2. **Every unvisited note is a faded neutral grey,** clearly dimmer than today's `#5b6584` Plain colour. Only what the session visited carries colour.
3. **Size means how often a note is visited:** the number of captured sessions that read it (the `sessions` field already on each note), with total reads shown in the tooltip. The arc intent's point 3 said size shows sharing (links in). Keep that as a "Size by: Visits | Links in" toggle and default to Visits, because that is the owner's call.
4. **A peek draws no line.** A `front_matter_read` only colours its note. An agent's path joins its FULL reads only, as jumps (or a walk when a full read's recorded parent is the same agent). This removes the solid fans, because those rules are recorded as peeks.

**His conflict question is answered in chat, and the data is worth showing.** Many active decisions and few superseded follows from the house rule that an overtaken claim is corrected IN PLACE when the decision itself did not change, while supersession is kept for real re-decisions. Granularity also keeps most decisions from overlapping. If cheap, compute and show one visible form of tension: active notes whose links still point at a superseded decision (stale support edges). His picture of 0.3 (dense under each story, sparse between) is what this placement draws once notes are tied to work, which ADR-0624's default link does.

**How to run it:**
- Export from a 0.2 checkout: `pnpm -C packages/cli exec node --import ../../scripts/tsx-cache-off.mjs --import tsx ~/.storytree/prototypes/planet-core/export-corpus.mts`. It needs the live store.
- Then `node build.mjs` and `node measure.mjs`.
- Check locally with `serve.mjs` on 127.0.0.1:5391 and `preview_start {url}`. The pane is hidden, so shim `requestAnimationFrame` with `setTimeout` and call `window.__planet.kick()`.
- Take screenshots with `shoot.mjs`.
- Republish `dist/index.html` to https://claude.ai/artifact/RSeesuTgNM7Xy9aALgN2Sz. From a new conversation, read that artifact first, then publish with its `url`.

**Close:** update `oq-planet-prototype-look`'s context to the new version, close this increment with a note, and release claims. Acting on his yes / no / not yet stays with `-inc-02`.
fields.title: Prototype pass 3 from the owner's second look

outcome.note:
**Pass 3 is published as version 4** of https://claude.ai/artifact/RSeesuTgNM7Xy9aALgN2Sz, the same private link. The source and README are in `~/.storytree/prototypes/planet-core/`, and nothing was committed to 0.2 or 0.3. It was checked in the Browser pane against a local copy of the same file, and in a clean Playwright run with no page errors: the four changes, the Forest / Library / Both toggle, the size toggle, every colouring, hovering and pinning a ghost, the neighbourhood filter, and phone width.

**What changed, per the owner's second look:**
- Superseded and proposed decisions are back as ghosts: see-through bubbles, about 20% opaque, that light in the reader's colour when read. 53 superseded ones sit beside the current decision that replaced them (following chains of replacement), 2 ride beside a replacement that orbits, and the 10 proposed ones sit near the notes they link to. The card names the replacement: `supersedes` inverted, counting decided records only, as `supersededDecisionNumbers` does, and the export stops if the inversion disagrees with any derived status. Active depth, links and reach are still computed over active notes only, and the ghosts do not change the active layout.
- A note the session did not read is a faded neutral grey (`#3a3d46`, was `#5b6584`).
- Size is visits (captured sessions that read the note), with a "Size by: Visits | Links in" toggle and total reads in the tooltip.
- A peek draws no line: each agent's path joins its full reads only. Checked per session: every drawn segment belongs to a full read, and none to a peek.
- A fifth colouring, "Stale links", shows active notes whose links still point at a superseded decision.

**What it showed:**
- No full read in the eight sessions was reached by a recorded link. Every recorded walk leads to a peek (an agent pulling in its standing rules), so under the owner's rule every remaining line is a jump.
- "Chapter 2 archival and MVP rebuild" read ghosts 43 times, on 9 distinct ghosts, and all 9 light. Its agents' most-read ghost is ADR-0003, superseded by ADR-0500.
- Stale links: 38 active notes (24 of them decisions) still link to 21 of the 55 superseded decisions, over 41 links; 7 active notes link to a proposed decision. This is the data behind the answer to his conflict question: supersession is kept for real re-decisions, and an overtaken claim is corrected in place.
- The two most-visited notes are `plan` (407 sessions) and `merge-ceremony` (326); the third is read in 91.

`oq-planet-prototype-look`'s context now describes version 4. Acting on his yes / no / not yet stays with `-inc-02`, which also waits on `oq-0-3-read-record-names-the-agent`.

fields.body:
*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this increment was `storytree-0-3-first-users-arc-inc-01`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

Owner exploration, not a decision (he is new to chaos-driven development and asked whether it applies). Chaos testing breaks the RUNNING system on purpose — kill a process, stop the database, stall a call, run two things at once — and checks it recovers; mutation testing breaks the CODE to check the TESTS. The case for it here: nearly every expensive 0.2 incident was operational and no unit test could have caught it (the git clean that recursed through junctions, database cold starts, hung writes committing late over newer edits, orphaned gates, concurrent gates on the shared box). Candidate seams in 0.3: local Postgres down or slow at start; the hook process killed mid-write; the MCP server restarted while an agent holds a session; the test runner hanging when storytree verifies red-green itself; two projects open at once. Dependency: it starts once cutover lands (`0-3-cutover-builds-itself`, now on `storytree-0-3-cutover-arc`; an increment gate records the wait). *(Corrected in place 2026-09-27: this used to say it starts once `trusted-circle-distribution-arc` closes. That founding arc was retired the same day, after all its other work had moved to lane arcs or landed, so the wait now names cutover itself.)* The library and its local Postgres are already built. Moved 2026-09-26 from `minimal-viable-tdd-arc-inc-03` (withdrawn there as moved); the standard it serves is ADR-0623. Deliverable: a short list of drills, each naming the incident class it would have caught and what it costs to run — or a recorded decline. Must not grow into a framework; a drill that needs infrastructure larger than the seam it tests is itself the bloat this arc exists to stop.

*Moved from storytree 0.2's library at cutover (2026-09-27), where this increment was `storytree-0-3-arc-surface-arc-inc-01`. ADR numbers in this text are 0.2's decision numbers; 0.2's copy stays readable there.*

This is the owner-gated first step, as it was for the library and the agent link (ADR-0625 D5). Draft the arc surface's capability tree:
- each capability in two plain sentences;
- what it depends on;
- how it will be proven, red then green;
- a simple diagram of how the parts connect.

The owner reads best from a private artifact page with a short Python sketch and an office analogy that says where it breaks.

**Put it to him, then END.** Author it as an `open-question` on this arc: `pnpm storytree question new --arc storytree-0-3-arc-surface-arc … --pg`. Never wait while holding a claim. Three reviews are being drafted at once (verified health, the arc surface and the forest), and he answers them one at a time, in his own order. That was the owner's selection on 2026-09-26: "Draft all 3 now, answer 1 at a time". So a draft may wait in his queue, and that is expected.

**Questions the tree must answer:**
- How each story's planned, in-progress or landed state is derived from the records: claims, landings and health.
- How "by which agent" is shown, from the agent link's sessions and claims.
- How it shares the project switcher with the forest (`storytree-0-3-forest-arc`), whose review is being drafted at the same time.
- The one 0.2 render not to port, recorded in `0-3-arc-surface`'s body: a row waiting on the owner must never also read as takeable.

**Read first:**
- ADR-0625: D3 story 3, and D8 (no increments in 0.3).
- ADR-0626, the agent link's sessions and claims.
- ADR-0621, the library API: `projectTree`, `arcsFor`, `changesSince` and `listProjects`.
- In the 0.3 repo (`C:\code\storytree03`): `stories/agent-link.md` and today's plain list in `apps/desktop`.
- 0.2's arc view is reference only: port behaviour, not code.

**When he approves:** record the tree as an ADR and settle the question in the same landing. The build is `0-3-arc-surface`, on this arc.

**Residue (2026-09-26, session "Draft the 0.3 arc-surface capability-tree review", branch `claude/dazzling-ramanujan-15fd62`).** The review is drafted and put to the owner, and this increment now waits on his answer.
- **The question:** `oq-0-3-arc-surface-capability-tree` (now revision 4), on this arc. The owner's readable copy is the private page https://claude.ai/artifact/N8tuscjiftPadHGDJFkLjP, updated in place.
- **Revision 2, same day, after the owner's first read**, in his words: "B and D make sense, 2 and 3 feel like one capability for agent claims to the board - why did you think unplanned activity needed its own. arcs page should probably arcs surface and probably should also have 5 folded into it? what are your thoughts". He did not approve the tree yet. B1 and D1 are his.
- **Revision 3, same day**, for two reasons:
  - The owner dropped verified health from the MVP (ADR-0630), so choice C was reframed. C1, recommended, shows the agent's own report only, labelled as the agent's, and does not draw the verified column.
  - The owner asked: "what about arc dependencies? or have we not scoped that for MVP". That became choice F. They are not in the MVP; 0.3 records only part-to-part dependencies. F1, recommended, shows those, across stories too, adding one proof to Arc surface.
  - The verified-health lane's note, prepended to the question's statement at 09:38, is carried into revision 3's text.
- **Revision 4, same day:** aligned with the forest review the owner approved (ADR-0632).
  - The switcher, the Forest | Arcs toggle and the opening project moved to the new 0.3 app story (`storytree-0-3-app-arc`, ADR-0632 D4).
  - "Unplanned activity" is renamed "unclaimed work" (ADR-0632 D5).
  - C3 now follows the forest drill-down's rule (storytree's column only where something wrote it).
- **The tree now proposed:** three capabilities, built in the order 1 → 3, with 14 contracts in all:
  1. Work states: planned, in progress or landed, for each part and each story, from the log's claimed and landed lines.
  2. Agents on the board (revision 1's "Who is on it" and "Unplanned activity" merged): who holds each part, read through the agent link's own claim reading (harness, when the window opened, reason, active or idle), plus edits made with nothing claimed (unclaimed work).
  3. Arc surface (revision 1's "Arcs page" with "Live feed" folded in): the per-project page, grown out of today's plain list. It shows the agent's own health report (C1), and each part names the parts it waits on, in any story (F1). It stays current through the app's live reading: the main process opens the agent log beside the library and uses `changesSince`, the log's cursor and a once-a-minute re-judge.

  "approve" now takes C1, E1 and F1. A, B (B1) and D (D1) are settled by his first read.
- **Boundaries agreed with the sibling lanes on 2026-09-26** (by message; both sessions confirmed):
  - **Forest** (approved as ADR-0632, whose D3 records these):
    - Work states (1) and the arc surface's live reading (part of 3) are this tree's, and the forest uses them. It reads Work states per part. In revision 1 these were "Work states (1) and Live feed (5)"; the forest session was told the new names.
    - Whichever view lands first retires today's plain list, and whichever lands second adds the Forest | Arcs toggle, under the 0.3 app story's name.
    - If the forest lands first, it builds these under this tree's names.
    - Both views show the same cross-story part dependencies, and both say "unclaimed work".
  - **The 0.3 app** (new story, ADR-0632 D4, arc `storytree-0-3-app-arc`): it owns the switcher, the toggle, hosting the views and which project opens first. This tree uses its switcher, and both views use today's dropdown until it is built.
  - **Verified health:** the boundary agreed with that lane (it would write only the verified column, with a "checking" note) no longer applies. The owner dropped verified health from the MVP (ADR-0630), and its lane closed with nothing built.
- **If he approves:**
  - Record the tree as an ADR in his words (`adr new --decided`).
  - Settle the question in the same landing (`question settle … --adr <n>`).
  - Write the tree up as `stories/arc-surface.md` in the 0.3 repo, and build `0-3-arc-surface` red→green in the order 1 → 3, landing through pull requests.
- **If he reshapes it again:** revise the question in place as the next revision, and republish the page at the same URL.
- **Reading `arc show` meanwhile:** 0.2's arc view prints both "waiting on the owner … held" and "`active` but NO claim holds it … Takeable" for this increment. That is exactly the 0.2 render this story exists not to port. The waiting line is the true one: nothing here is work to take until he answers.
- Nothing was built and nothing was committed (ADR-0625 D5).

**Owner, round 3 (2026-09-26, on revision 4), verbatim:** "should be a overlay over the forest is that still what we going for, we dont need to reinvent this from 0.2 the arc surface was working quite well in 0.2. I want arc dependancies and increment dependancies in the MVP i think its important. Any more questions?"
- **Settled by it:**
  - E: the arc surface is an OVERLAY over the forest, as 0.2's arc surface was a top-drawer lens over the map. This replaces E1's separate view with a toggle.
  - Port 0.2's arc surface behaviour: one lane per arc, a bar per unit, queued arcs nested under their blocker, a briefing panel for the selected arc, and read-only.
  - F: arc dependencies AND increment dependencies are in the MVP (F2 widened). **ADR-0628 D6**, decided the same day and missed by revisions 1–4, already fixes the 0.3 grain:
    - a story on one arc can wait on a story on another arc;
    - it shows as queued until that story lands;
    - the wait releases on landing, and keeps holding (and says so) if the blocker was retired unlanded;
    - loops are refused when written;
    - the wait is kept apart from code dependencies.

    Arc waits port ADR-0523's arc gate. Both need the library to store them (an extension to its capability 4, the work model) and the agent link's planning tools to set them (an extension to its capability 6).
- **Put back to him in chat:**
  - **Q1.** 0.3 records no open questions. Should the overlay's briefing show only the arc's description, or should 0.3 gain questions that agents raise and settle, shown yellow as "waiting on you"? Recommended: gain them, since cutover moves 0.3's own reviews into 0.3.
  - **Q2.** Does a story's wait refuse an agent's claim on its parts, the 0.3 analogue of ADR-0628 D3's start refusal, or only show? Recommended: refuse, naming the blocker.
- **Next:** revision 5 after his answers. The likely tree is Work states, Waits (new), Agents on the board, and Arc surface (the overlay, with lanes). When recorded, the overlay annotates ADR-0632 D3/D4's "Forest | Arcs toggle" in place, and the app story's review hosts an arcs overlay rather than a toggle.

**Owner, round 4 (2026-09-26), verbatim:** "isn't an arc made up of increments, where did this arc is a list of stories come from? Yes open questions should also make it to 0.3 mvp. Yes refuse the claim."
- **Answered:**
  - Q1 = (b): open questions are in the 0.3 MVP.
  - Q2 = (a): a wait refuses the claim, naming the blocker.
- **Provenance he asked for:**
  - "Arc = a list of stories" entered through ADR-0621. Its option B1 settled only that stories belong to the project and an arc MAY list them. Its D6 "left out" list then named "arc increments", a line the drafting session wrote.
  - ADR-0625 D8 spelled out the consequence ("no separate increments inside 0.3"). The signed spec page listed it among the changes his signature covered. He never chose it in his own words.
- **Put back to him:** bring increments back into 0.3 (an arc holds increments, as in 0.2)? Recommended yes. It would:
  - reverse ADR-0625 D8 and ADR-0621 D6's "arc increments" exclusion;
  - return ADR-0628 D6's 0.3 grain to increment-waits-on-increment.

  It would add an increment record and a question record to the library, plus planning, gate, question and claim tools to the agent link. The arc surface's bars would become increments, a straight port of 0.2's lanes.

**Owner, round 5 (2026-09-26), verbatim:** "yes bring increments back. Is there anything else we have decided to bring back in only bits for 0.3? just want to make sure theres nothing unintentional i've signed off on"
- **Decided:** increments come back into 0.3 (an arc holds increments). This reverses ADR-0625 D8 and ADR-0621 D6's "arc increments" exclusion, and returns ADR-0628 D6's grain to increment-waits-on-increment.
- **Audit answered in chat.** Every 0.3 decision (ADR-0621 to ADR-0632) was checked for 0.2 behaviour taken only in part through agent-written lines. Flagged for his pick:
  1. decision status and supersession (ADR-0621 D6);
  2. decision numbers (ADR-0621 D6);
  3. the knowledge kinds left out (ADR-0621 D6);
  4. arcs' lifecycle and fields (the ADR-0621 schema);
  5. 0.3's own stories and decisions written as repo files and copied in by `pnpm seed:library`, against ADR-0621 D6's "the library is the only copy";
  6. increment claims (ADR-0626 D9; returns with increments);
  7. no command line for people (ADR-0621 D6, ADR-0626 D9);
  8. a 0.3 librarian that ADR-0631 relies on and nothing schedules;
  9. claims not ending on a PR merge (ADR-0626 D9);
  10. which parts of increments and questions return (for revision 5).
- **Next:** revision 5 after his picks.

**Owner, round 6 (2026-09-26), verbatim:** "All 9 need to be brought in, cuts should only be made by explicit decision by me, 0.2 worked well we shouldnt cut the parts that worked into bits, it should be easy to bring this stuff over as I'm sure we exposing our builders with the ability to refer to 0.2 code and corpus to bring it over."
- **Recorded as ADR-0633** (accepted, load-bearing in effect).
  - D1: no cut without his explicit decision; an agent-written "left out" line is only a proposal.
  - D2: builders port from 0.2's code and corpus.
  - D3: 14 items back in the MVP whole, including increments, open questions, arc and increment waits, a wait refusing a claim, and the arc surface as an overlay.
  - D4: every other agent-written cut is in `oq-0-3-cuts-awaiting-owner-decision` on `trusted-circle-distribution-arc`.
  - D5: routing, parked as four increments: `0-3-library-tree-for-adr-0633`, `0-3-agent-link-tree-for-adr-0633`, `0-3-library-is-the-one-copy` and `0-3-librarian-home`.
  - In-place notes in ADR-0621, 0625, 0626, 0628, 0631 and 0632, written by a librarian subagent in the same landing.
- **This session handed over at the context mark** (711K of the ~700K soft mark). Revision 5 is for a FRESH session.
- **REVISION 5 BRIEF (for the next session on this increment):**
  - **Port 0.2's arc surface WHOLE, as an overlay over the forest** (until the forest lands, over today's plain list). Read the behaviour from 0.2's code:
    - `apps/studio/src/components/ArcSurface.tsx`, `apps/studio/src/lib/arcSurface.ts` and `packages/arc/src/arc-rollup.ts`;
    - ADR-0314 (lanes and briefing), ADR-0523 (arc gate, nesting), ADR-0574 (waiting on the owner, yellow), ADR-0628 (increment gates) and ADR-0564 (what a close meant).
  - **What the port carries:**
    - one lane per arc, one bar per INCREMENT (arcs hold increments again);
    - lane states: waiting on the owner, blocked, claimed, unknown, quiet, parked and closed;
    - queued arcs nested under their blocker;
    - a briefing panel with the arc's description and open questions;
    - claim chips per arc, read-only, kept live.
  - **Settled and still binding:**
    - D1: idle never reads as free;
    - B1: in progress means started and not landed, now at increment grain too;
    - a wait refuses a claim (enforced by the agent link);
    - Work states and the live reading stay shared with the forest (ADR-0632 D3).
  - **Still open for him:** C (health beside the state; C1 recommended). E and F are superseded by the overlay and ADR-0633.
  - **The tree must follow `capabilities-name-durable-functions-decisions-go-on-shelves`,** and put every remaining 0.2 piece not ported as a NAMED choice (ADR-0633 D1).
  - **Agree boundaries** with the library's and the agent link's tree revisions above.
  - **Revise `oq-0-3-arc-surface-capability-tree` in place as revision 5,** and republish its page at https://claude.ai/artifact/N8tuscjiftPadHGDJFkLjP. Fetch its current HTML with the Artifact tool's read action on that URL, then publish back with `url`.


**Owner, round 7 (2026-09-26), verbatim:** "C0, A". He typed it in the drafting session (desktop title "Draft the 0.3 arc-surface capability-tree review"), choosing from two options that session composed, and that session relayed it to revision 5's session by message; the words were checked against its transcript.
- **C0:** no health on the overlay, as in 0.2. Health stays with the forest (its leaves and drill-down, ADR-0632). Choice C is closed.
- **A:** 0.2's increment lifecycle is kept, and a proposal counts as waiting on the owner. The option text said 0.2 shows a proposal "yellow beside open questions (ADR-0359)". 0.2 as built does not: a proposal draws grey, its lane does not read waiting, and its briefing's proposal list was cut at the owner's word in 0.2 ("I never read the proposals so we should drop that part of the surface"). Revision 5 records A as he read it (yellow, listed under "Waiting on you", lane reads waiting) and gives him a one-word exit, "A as built".

**Residue (2026-09-26, session `sleepy-wright-b57669`, branch `claude/pensive-wilson-369e7b`): revision 5 is drafted and put to the owner.**
- **The question:** `oq-0-3-arc-surface-capability-tree`, revised in place (store seq 21129). His readable copy is https://claude.ai/artifact/N8tuscjiftPadHGDJFkLjP, now version 6.
- **The tree:** five capabilities and 23 contracts, built 1 → 2 → 3, then 4 and 5:
  1. Work states: parts (revision 4's rule, which the forest reads), increments (one reading, first match: waiting on the owner, then queued, then held, then open) and arcs (0.2's seven lane states, in 0.2's order);
  2. Agents on the board: who holds each increment and part, live or idle. Unclaimed work moved to the forest (its capability 6);
  3. Arc surface: the overlay itself, a lane per arc and a bar per increment, counts never a percentage, lane chips, Active/Parked/Closed, and the live reading;
  4. Waits: queued arcs fold under their blocker, and queued increments name their blocker;
  5. Briefing: the intent, then open questions and proposals under "Waiting on you", then settled questions with their answers.

  Work states is still capability 1 and the live reading still part of capability 3, so ADR-0632 D3's references hold.
- **Open for the owner:** Q, a queued increment's colour (Q1, 0.2's queued-arc clay, recommended) and L, the floor-health lamp (ADR-0314 D7; L1, later, recommended). "approve" takes Q1, L1 and every proposed book.
- **Boundaries:** aligned with the forest (ADR-0632) and the app (ADR-0634). The library's and agent link's sides are PROPOSED and written onto `0-3-library-tree-for-adr-0633` and `0-3-agent-link-tree-for-adr-0633`, because no session held either. The main proposals: the library owns the one reading of whether a wait holds and whether an increment waits on the owner; the agent link's refusal also covers work waiting on the owner.
- **When he approves:** record the tree as an ADR in his words (`adr new --decided`) and settle the question in the same landing. Annotate ADR-0632 D2 in place: its "Cross-story capability links are shown, the same ones the arc surface shows" no longer holds, because the overlay shows increments, not part links. Write `stories/arc-surface.md` in the 0.3 repo. The build `0-3-arc-surface` needs the library's and agent link's revised trees for increments, questions, waits and increment claims; Work states at part grain (what the forest's capability 2 reads), and the live reading, need neither, so they can start first.
- **If he reshapes it:** revise the question in place as revision 6 and republish the page at the same URL.
- Nothing was built and nothing was committed (ADR-0625 D5).

**Owner, round 8 (2026-09-27), verbatim, in session `sleepy-wright-b57669`:** "Follow 0.2, a proposal shouldnt wait for my yes, proposal means not built yet doesnt mean waiting on me, else I end up having to say "build it" to things i directed to be built."
- **A is settled as 0.2 has it:** a proposal means not built yet. It draws grey, is not listed in the briefing, and never makes its arc read waiting. "Waiting on the owner" means only work held on a question he has not answered (ADR-0574).
- **Revision 6** records it (store seq 21148; page version 7, same URL). It withdraws revision 5's proposals that the agent link refuse a claim on an unapproved proposal and ready a proposal only on his say-so. The boundary notes on `0-3-agent-link-tree-for-adr-0633` and `0-3-library-tree-for-adr-0633` are corrected to match.
- **Still open:** Q and L. The residue above otherwise holds, reading "revision 6" for "revision 5".

**Owner, round 9 (2026-09-27), verbatim:** "increment waiting on other work should show up yellow. whats the floor hearlth lamp?"
- **Q is settled:** an increment that cannot start because of a wait (its own, or its arc's) draws yellow, like work held on his question; the hover names what it waits for. 0.2's clay bar colour for a queued arc is not used; the lane's arrow and "blocked" chip still show a whole arc waiting. Revision 7 (store seq 21161; page version 8).
- **L is the one choice left.** He asked what the lamp is; it was explained in chat and he has not decided.

**Owner, round 10 (2026-09-27), verbatim:** "bring it back later it needs rework anyway, in 0.2 i never really saw it light up and never really use it, the concept is right the implementation needs rework"
- **L is settled:** the floor-health lamp is neither in the MVP overlay nor cut. It is parked on this arc as `0-3-floor-health-lamp-reworked`, for after first users, with its own review before code.
- **Revision 8** (page version 9) has every choice settled. What remains is his approval of the tree ("approve"). When it comes: record the tree as an ADR in his words, settle the question in the same landing, annotate ADR-0632 D2, and write `stories/arc-surface.md` (see the residue above).

**Owner, round 11 (2026-09-27), verbatim:** "for increment state can we get rid of withdraw and closed these should be folded into red - red is anything that failed to complete or was not completed. Yellow is waiting or blocked. sessions/agents claim the whole arc right not sure why we have increment level agent holds?"
- **Decided:** four increment colours. Green landed; red anything not completed (failed, withdrawn, closed with nothing recorded); yellow waiting or blocked; grey open. The record keeps the kind of close (ADR-0564) and the hover shows it. Revision 9 (store seq after 21167; page version 10). Proposed with it: lane chips "waiting" and "blocked" yellow.
- **Asked, not yet decided:** why increment-level holds. Answered in chat: in 0.2 agents claim capabilities, falling back to the increment when there is no capability to name; whole-arc claims are rare (about 5% of holds, per 0.2's arcSurface.ts). Increment claims entered 0.3 through ADR-0633 D3 item 10. The overlay's per-bar holder mark is this review's own proposal (new, not 0.2). Awaiting his call.

**Owner, round 12 (2026-09-27), verbatim:** "right this makes sense, i'm fine with increment level claims then." after the flow was explained (an arc reads "claimed" when a live session holds any claim on its work: an increment of it, a capability one of its increments builds, or rarely the arc itself; capability claims stop double-building, increment claims stop two sessions driving one unit, and arcs stay open to several sessions at once).

**What the tree must answer:**
- **Depth.** The longest chain of links down from a shelf's front covers (ADR-0476 D2), using the library's `frontCovers()` and its note-to-note links (`0-3-library-knowledge-entrances`, built). A shortest-chain reading would flatten the core. Notes no shelf reaches have no depth and orbit outside, never at the centre.
- **Loops.** 0.3 lets notes link in loops, so depth needs a stated rule for one (0.2 carried a `cyclic` state). No rule exists yet; propose one.
- **Ghosts.** 0.3's library carries no decision status (ADR-0621 D6, reaffirmed by ADR-0627 D6). A replaced decision is one whose front-cover mark was cleared when a new cover linking to it took its place, which the library's write history shows. Draw those as see-through ghosts beside their replacement, lit when read. 0.3 has no proposed state, so there are no proposed ghosts. Put this to him as a proposal, since version 4 drew both kinds from 0.2's data.
- **Reads.** Visits (how many sessions read a note) and each session's trail come from the agent link's read record, in its agent activity log (ADR-0626 D2). Nothing yet reads that log back by session and agent in time order; a young project's log is small, so reading the whole of it may do at first. A peek lights its note and draws no line; full reads join as jumps, and a line is drawn only for a link the record says was followed (ADR-0624 D3). Each agent gets its own colour when the record names it (`0-3-agent-link-read-record-names-the-agent`); a read whose agent is "unknown" is drawn pale and draws no path.
- **What carries over from version 4.** Size by visits with a links-in toggle, faded grey for unread notes, links shown only for a pinned note, and possibly the stale-links view. He asked for each of these on 0.2's data; confirm them for 0.3.
